ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary AML/CFT legislation is Law 10/2010 of 28 April on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended, including by Royal Decree-Law 7/2021 and subsequent implementing measures. Core implementing regulation is Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May. Beneficial-ownership registration and access rules are principally governed by Royal Decree 609/2023 of 11 July, establishing the Central Register of Real Ownership (Registro Central de Titularidades Reales, RCTIR), together with Law 10/2010, the Spanish Companies Act approved by Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010, and applicable Mercantile Registry rules. The entity must identify natural persons who directly or indirectly hold more than 25 percent of ownership or voting rights or otherwise exercise control; where no such person can be identified, the senior managing official is recorded as the fallback beneficial owner. The legal analysis must also apply the control and ownership tests in Article 4 of Law 10/2010 and its implementing regulation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry or equivalent corporate authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing country is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization through the issuing authority, the competent foreign ministry and the competent Spanish diplomatic or consular mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry, notary or competent corporate authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where available; otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity document of each director, shareholder and identified beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent identity-document authority in the country of issuance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy followed by Hague Apostille where accepted, or Consular Legalization where apostille is unavailable; Spanish notarial certification may also be required for the incorporation file

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney for incorporation, tax registration and bank-account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where available; otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization where executed outside Spain; Spanish translation by a sworn translator may be required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Tax authority in the country of tax residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where available; otherwise Consular Legalization; official Spanish translation may be required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, the notary, bank, payment institution and regulated professional advisers should screen the company, directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, authorized signatories, counterparties and relevant family members or close associates against United Nations Security Council lists, EU restrictive-measures lists, Spanish domestic sanctions and terrorist-financing lists, and relevant commercial sanctions databases. OFAC screening is not generally a standalone Spanish statutory requirement but is required where there is a United States nexus, United States financial institution exposure, United States-dollar clearing or contractual compliance obligation. PEP identification, enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, senior-management approval, enhanced monitoring and documented risk assessment are required under Law 10/2010 for domestic and foreign PEPs and their family members and known close associates. Sanctions are strict-liability risk controls requiring escalation, transaction blocking where legally required, and reporting to the competent authority. Records and AML evidence should generally be retained for ten years under Law 10/2010.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central electronic services portal (RMC), accessible through https://sede.registradores.org
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must include the legal-form designation Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada or the abbreviation Sociedad Limitada or S.L. The name must be sufficiently distinct from existing registered or reserved names and must not be misleading, unlawful, offensive or confusingly similar. Spanish company names are ordinarily recorded using the Latin alphabet; foreign words, abbreviations and transliterations may be used if legally acceptable and not deceptive. A certificate of name availability from the Registro Mercantil Central is required before execution of the incorporation deed. The notary and Registro Mercantil may reject names that imply regulated activities, public authority, official status, geographic endorsement or a business activity not actually authorized.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Submit an electronic application to the Registro Mercantil Central for a certificate of name availability, normally proposing up to five alternatives. After issuance, deliver the certificate to the Spanish notary for incorporation within its statutory validity period. The statutory certificate validity is generally three months from issuance for execution of the incorporation deed, while the name may be renewable for an additional period under Mercantile Registry rules; the 30-day value in this dossier is an internal filing-control deadline and must not replace verification of the certificate's stated expiry date. If rejected, obtain the written reason, correct the proposed name or submit alternative names, and file a request for review or appeal with the Registro Mercantil Central within the applicable administrative period. A final administrative decision may be challenged before the competent administrative court under Spanish administrative-procedure and contentious-administrative rules. A rejection based on similarity, prohibited terminology or legal-form noncompliance is normally best addressed by submitting materially different alternatives rather than litigating.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Spanish Sociedad Limitada must have a registered office in Spain under the Spanish Companies Act. A virtual office may be acceptable for corporate registration if it is a genuine address capable of receiving official notices and maintaining corporate records, but it does not by itself establish operational substance. For a cross-border parcel-consolidation hub, the company should maintain a real operating address, documented warehouse or handling arrangements, logistics contracts, personnel or outsourced-service evidence, customs and transport records, insurance, and local management capacity. A virtual office is high-risk where it is used as the apparent location of warehousing, parcel handling, customs activity, payment operations or regulated logistics functions. The company must also assess municipal activity licences, premises-use rules, fire and occupational-safety requirements, waste obligations, data-protection compliance, consumer rules and any customs or transport registrations applicable to the actual services.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection is approximately 2 to 8 percent for a newly incorporated, low-risk logistics company with no customs, excise, cash-intensive or regulated financial activity and a credible registered office. Estimated probability may increase to approximately 10 to 25 percent during the first three years if the company declares warehouse operations, handles imported parcels, uses a virtual office, claims material VAT refunds, has inconsistent operational data, or is selected for tax, labour, customs, municipal or AML review. These are non-statutory risk estimates, not official Spanish inspection statistics.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), particularly Articles 4, 20-23, 28-30, 32-35, 58-62, 210-242 and 249; supplemented by the Commercial Registry Regulations approved by Royal Decree 1784/1996 and Law 14/2013 on entrepreneurs and CIRCE procedures.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the company's registered office; the Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) issues the name-clearance certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución) filed for registration with the competent Provincial Commercial Registry, supported by the certified company-name certificate and bank certificate or founder declaration evidencing the capital contribution.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The minimum capital of a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. Until equity reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve and shareholders have additional liability up to the difference between EUR 3,000 and the subscribed capital upon liquidation. A statutory escrow account is not mandatory; a bank certificate may evidence cash contributions, and founders may instead declare responsibility for the contribution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board resolves that: (1) the Company accepts and ratifies the subscription and full payment of its issued share capital by the founding shareholder in accordance with the public deed; (2) the registered office at [full Spanish address] is adopted and recorded; (3) [name] is appointed sole director, or the persons listed in Schedule 1 are appointed as directors, each accepting office and declaring no legal incompatibility; (4) the appointed representative is authorized to obtain the NIF, complete Commercial Registry filings, open operating bank accounts, and execute documents required for commencement of business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), its online name-certification service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed names, identifying the founder and intended company form. Obtain the original certificate of negative denomination. Reserve and use the name within its statutory validity period, and deliver the certificate to the notary.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected, submit an alternative name or an appeal supported by evidence of distinctiveness. Correct spelling, legal-form, or identity inconsistencies before requesting a new certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare founder, capital, and registered-office documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary selected by the founders; collaborating bank where a cash contribution certificate is requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain NIEs for non-resident founders and directors where required. Prepare bylaws, ownership percentages, management structure, business purpose, registered-office evidence, and capital contribution records. Foreign corporate documents must generally be apostilled or legalized, translated into Spanish by a sworn translator, and accompanied by evidence of signatory authority.
required_dossiers: Founders' passports or national identity documents
Foreign shareholder constitutional documents and incumbency evidence, if applicable
Bank certificate or founder contribution declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure documentary defects by notarized supplementary instruments, corrected sworn translations, renewed apostilles, or additional corporate-authority evidence. Replace expired name or bank certificates where necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the public deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear personally or through a notarized power of attorney. Execute the escritura pública de constitución containing the company name, purpose, registered office, capital, share allocation, bylaws, management system, and initial director appointment. The notary verifies identity, authority, legal capacity, and beneficial-owner information.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Execute a corrective or supplementary deed for omissions or inconsistencies. If the notary refuses authorization, request written grounds and resubmit after curing the identified legal or documentary defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain provisional tax identification and register the deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria), using Form 036 or CIRCE/PAE; competent Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request the provisional NIF and file the incorporation deed electronically or through the notarial CIRCE channel. Pay applicable notarial and registry charges. Submit the deed, name certificate, bylaws, tax forms, and beneficial-owner information to the registry for review and registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a qualification notice, correct the stated defect through a supplementary deed or supporting document and resubmit within the applicable legal period. Challenge a refusal before the Directorate-General for Legal Security and Public Faith or the competent court, as applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-registration tax and governance formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency; Provincial Commercial Registry; Social Security General Treasury (Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the definitive NIF, file the commencement and census details, register beneficial ownership where required, legalize accounting and corporate books electronically, and register as an employer before hiring personnel. Adopt the first board or shareholder resolutions and establish banking and accounting controls.
required_dossiers: Employer registration documents, if employees are hired
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected tax or Social Security filings through the relevant electronic portal. File late registrations with applicable explanations and settle statutory surcharges or penalties where imposed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Secure site-specific logistics and premises approvals
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal authority (Ayuntamiento) at the warehouse location; relevant Autonomous Community authority where regional environmental or industrial authorization applies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before occupying or operating the hub, verify zoning compatibility and submit the applicable responsible declaration, prior communication, or activity-opening license under municipal rules and Law 12/2012. Obtain construction or fit-out permits where required. Confirm that the activity does not constitute regulated carriage, waste treatment, customs warehousing, or another separately licensed activity.
required_dossiers: Environmental or waste documentation, if applicable
Responsible declaration or municipal license application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to municipal technical queries, amend the technical report, cure deficiencies, or request an inspection. Appeal a refusal through the applicable administrative review and judicial-administrative procedures.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The Ayuntamiento of the warehouse municipality is the primary authority for activity, opening, zoning, and premises approvals; the competent Autonomous Community industrial and environmental department applies where regional authorization is triggered. No general national manufacturing license is required for ordinary parcel consolidation and sorting.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal activity and opening authorization (licencia de actividad y apertura), or responsible declaration/prior communication (declaración responsable/comunicación previa), depending on the municipality and facility characteristics.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: The environmental authority of the relevant Autonomous Community, applying Law 21/2013 on Environmental Assessment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally Exempt or outside the listed EIA categories for an ordinary indoor parcel sorting and consolidation hub without industrial processing, subject to site-specific screening. A full or simplified assessment may apply if the project involves listed land development, major construction, protected areas, significant storage, or other Annex I or II triggers.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No general process wastewater or VOC limit is created solely by parcel sorting. Sanitary and cleaning wastewater must comply with municipal sewer bylaws and any discharge permit. Fuels, batteries, chemicals, packaging, and damaged goods must be stored and managed under applicable waste and hazardous-waste rules. Noise, dust, vehicle emissions, and waste segregation must comply with municipal and Autonomous Community requirements. Waste operators and waste producers must register or maintain documentation where legally triggered.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The premises must comply with the Spanish Building Code, including fire-safety requirements, and the Industrial Safety Regulations for Fire Protection in Industrial Establishments (Royal Decree 2267/2004) where applicable. Obtain municipal fire-safety review or certification, maintain emergency routes and fire systems, and complete structural and floor-load verification for racking and parcel equipment. Comply with Law 31/1995 on Occupational Risk Prevention, including risk assessment, training, emergency planning, contractor coordination, and workplace health and safety controls.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Sede Electrónica del AEAT (https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) incorporated under Spanish law automatically receives a definitive corporate NIF (Código de Identificación Fiscal) with prefix 'B' upon provisional registration with the Mercantile Registry and final issuance by the AEAT. A foreign entity not established in Spain must obtain a non-resident NIF (NIF-N, format N or M prefixed) by applying through the AEAT, submitting the official form 036, a certificate of incorporation and proof of foreign tax residence, and appointing a Spanish tax representative for all tax obligations. For VAT purposes, the same NIF is used; non-established operators must additionally register under the special scheme for non-established taxable persons or the EU One Stop Shop (OSS) where applicable. Digital certificates (DNI electrónico, FNMT class 2) are required for electronic filings through the Sede Electrónica.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spanish tax law permits a fiscal consolidation election for groups of companies meeting common-control and ownership thresholds, allowing one consolidated tax base under the Corporate Income Tax (IS) regime. For EU entities, anti-hybrid and reverse hybrid rules under Directive (EU) 2016/1164 (ATAD) apply; there is no US-style check-the-box election, but taxpayers can elect special regimes such as the patent box, R&D deduction, and the territorial application of certain participation exemptions. The OSS non-union scheme election is available for pan-EU e-commerce VAT compliance.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (IVA - Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: General registration: compulsory for any person performing taxable supplies in Spanish territory without a threshold; the simplified scheme threshold is EUR 85,000 for eligible SMB businesses, and the SME annual turnover threshold is EUR 250,000 for certain special agricultural schemes. Distance sales into Spain from other EU states exceed EUR 10,000 annually to trigger Spanish VAT registration, while the EU-wide OSS threshold removes separate registrations up to EUR 10,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Large taxpayers (turnover exceeding EUR 6 million) must submit real-time invoice data under the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) through the AEAT's web service API; invoice issuance is based on digital stamps and X.509 certificates. For all other businesses, the 'Crea y Crece' law mandates the use of interoperable electronic invoicing programs; from 2025, software systems must comply with the Verifactu regulation, generating a standard SHA-256 hash and sending invoice records to AEAT on an immediate basis upon mandatory implementation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated VAT applies to: (1) the export of goods physically departing the EU to a third country or territory; (2) intra-EU dispatches to a VAT-registered customer in another Member State; (3) certain international services expressly listed in Ley 37/1992 (e.g., direct freight transport services related to exported goods, loading/unloading, storage incidental to exports). For parcel consolidation hubs, eligibility requires proof of physical export, commercial documentation evidencing title and destination, and that the goods leave the EU within a reasonable deadline (typically 3 months from dispatch).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA/SAD via TARIC and customs management system)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing departure from EU customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement proving receipt of foreign exchange from the destination country
Delivery evidence (e.g., PoD, e-commerce platform sales report, customs transit or exit notification from the cargo manifest)
Invoice and packing list referencing the export declaration number
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEAT can retroactively deny the zero rating and assess VAT at 21% plus applicable late-payment interest if export evidence is incomplete, or the 180-day repatriation deadline is breached without justified cause. Fraudulent export schemes, including fictitious removals, false declarations, or circular returns, are subject to tax penalty under Ley General Tributaria (LGT) from 50% to 150% of the tax base, with possible Article 258 criminal enforcement for evasion exceeding EUR 120,000, fines of up to six times the defrauded amount, and forfeiture of the refund claim. For interdisciplinary consolidated groups, the AEAT also applies substance-over-form rules to disregard shell arrangements used to fabricate export credentials.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain operates a fully convertible Euro currency regime for both current and capital accounts. Profit remittances to foreign shareholders are permitted following tax clearance and beneficial ownership verification. No capital controls or surrender requirements apply to resident companies for inbound or outbound FX transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds do not require mandatory surrender to the central bank. However, companies must report all foreign exchange transactions to the Banco de España through the reporting system and declare export revenues to the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) for VAT and corporate income tax purposes. Supporting documentation for all repatriated funds is mandatory under AML directives.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Airwallex and similar cross-border fintech platforms offer high viability for parcel consolidation operations due to local clearing integrations. However, legal constraints include mandatory Spanish entity registration for full services, compliance with MiCA if virtual assets involved, and integration with local payment systems like SEPA. Offshore digital EMIs require local bank partnerships or licensed intermediaries.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of directors or authorized representatives is mandatory for initial KYC interviews and corporate account opening at Spanish commercial banks. Remote onboarding is generally prohibited for new corporate clients without established relationships or specific regulatory exemptions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive beneficial ownership declaration, source of wealth documentation, and independent verification reports
Enhanced due diligence including third-party risk assessments and transaction pattern analysis

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections are routed via SWIFT MT103 or correspondent bank wires with purpose codes such as 'CAPITAL_CONTRIBUTION' or 'EQUITY_INJECTION'. Verification requires board resolutions, ownership certificates, and tax ID verification. All transactions must be reported to the Banco de España and AEAT for compliance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements utilize SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers, Commercial Letters of Credit (LCs) compliant with UCP 600, and SEPA Instant for eligible intra-EU payments. For non-EU destinations, correspondent banking networks are employed. Trade settlements require matching of invoices, shipping documents, and compliance with export/import formalities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval and deposit of annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must be approved within six months after the financial year-end and deposited within one month after approval. For a 31 December year-end, the usual deposit deadline is 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure may prevent registration of subsequent corporate filings. Administrative fines may be imposed, generally ranging from approximately EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, subject to statutory limits. Persistent non-compliance may result in an administrative penalty and registry-related enforcement; Spain does not apply an automatic annual franchise-tax strike-off rule.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the first 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the usual filing window is 1 to 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger statutory late-filing penalties, payment surcharges, and interest. A non-payment return filed without prior notice may generally attract a EUR 200 penalty, potentially reduced by 50% where the reduction conditions are satisfied. Tax underpayment may trigger surcharges of 1% plus 1% for each complete month of delay, subject to statutory maximums.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT summary return, Modelo 390, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally filed during the first 30 calendar days of January for the preceding calendar year. Certain taxpayers and filing profiles are exempt from Modelo 390.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing may attract a fixed tax penalty, generally EUR 200, subject to statutory reductions and proportionality rules. Inaccurate VAT filings may trigger additional assessment, interest, and tax penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership declaration and confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Relevant Mercantile Registry, through the annual accounts filing and applicable electronic forms
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Normally submitted with the annual accounts. Beneficial ownership information must also be updated without undue delay when ownership or control changes.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or report accurate beneficial ownership information may cause filing rejection, registry restrictions, and potential anti-money-laundering administrative sanctions. False or incomplete information may create additional corporate and director liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is generally mandatory when the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets above EUR 2.85 million, annual net turnover above EUR 5.7 million, or average employees above 50. Audit obligations also apply to certain public-interest entities, regulated activities, securities issuers, groups requiring consolidated accounts, and other statutory cases.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad), together with applicable Commercial Code and Companies Act requirements. IFRS is mandatory for specified consolidated-account situations and may apply where legally permitted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must identify, document, retain, and keep current its ultimate beneficial owners. The beneficial ownership declaration is normally confirmed or updated with the annual accounts filing. Any change in direct or indirect ownership or control must be reflected promptly, with supporting ownership and control documentation retained.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Sole-Shareholder Contracts, where the company has a sole shareholder
Beneficial ownership records and supporting identification and control evidence
Director appointment, authority, and Mercantile Registry records; Spain does not generally require a separate statutory book titled Register of Directors

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 325-1,300 annually for a registered office, local corporate secretarial support, and standard filing administration; actual pricing depends on location and service scope.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,000-8,000 for a small Spanish SL requiring a statutory audit; complex operations, group reporting, inventory, logistics activities, or extensive testing may materially increase the fee.
